audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is rated as a favoured lane — chart gives Fiora six of seven stages, difficulty 4/10, green tone, 'Favoured matchup' — on a 40.91% win rate over 264 games, and the content layer says the opposite from level 3 onward.
audit.why: whys[2] through whys[6], spikes[1..3], mid and late all describe Maokai stabilising with saplings and Sap Magic and then out-scaling; only whys[0] gives Fiora a window, with whys[1] a coinflip. packet.levelChart is Fiora, Skill, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai, Maokai.
audit.corrected: win[1]/phases[1] -> Skill; win[2..6] and phases[2..6] -> Maokai; diffRating 4/10 -> 8/10, tone to the hard-matchup red, and difficulty/report[14]/report[2]/tldr rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade when Twisted Advance is down' appears in a dozen fields with no number, and Nature's Grasp and Sapling Toss have no timings at all.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5; Fiora W is 24s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d now carry 14s, 18s, 130s and 24s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance makes Maokai UNTARGETABLE while he dashes, and no field says so. The page tells you to Riposte the root without saying that damage and abilities thrown at him mid-dash are simply lost.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' That splits the play in two — nothing lands during the dash; the parry has to cover the arrival.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[1].d now state the untargetable dash and that the parry target is the arrival root. The Riposte-returns-a-stun claim is CORRECT — the arrival root is an immobilizing effect.

edits.before: Riposte his root — vitals out-duel his tank kit. Fiora wins by trading around Maokai's Twisted Advance and cashing the pattern: riposte his root and out-duel with vitals.
edits.after: Parry the root or the lane is his — Twisted Advance is untargetable mid-dash, so Riposte the arrival, and know that after level 3 saplings and Sap Magic out-sustain your chip.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Twisted Advance and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 8/10. The lane is decided by whether you cash levels 1-2 before saplings and Sap Magic stabilise it.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Maokai carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10, Maokai carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Yours from level 1. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.
edits.after: His after level 3. See the level-by-level chart for the swing points.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Riposte it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1; he is untargetable mid-dash, so parry the arrival, not the cast. - Nature's Grasp: a 130s wall you cannot parry. - Riposte: 24s, saved for the root.

edits.after: His lock-on root — 14s at rank 1. Parry the arrival, not the dash.

edits.before: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Maokai, AA once, and E-slow out — repeat until his bar forces the all-in he loses.
edits.after: Twisted Advance makes him untargetable while he dashes — burst spent into it is lost; parry the root on arrival.

edits.before: Maokai wastes Twisted Advance (Root) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Maokai spends Twisted Advance — 14s of no lockdown. Commit the pattern.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Land Twisted Advance' and 'His Sapling Toss' — both FALSE POSITIVES, correct Riot names. This page was branded a favoured 4/10 lane on a 40.91% win rate; the content layer was already honest about it, so the mismatch was purely in the chart, the rating and the framing. Sap Magic heals off his basic attacks and its cooldown shortens every time he casts or is hit by a spell — report[8]'s early Executioner's Calling call is right for that reason.
